subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever persist doctor repairs automatically, and if so should the first implementation be an opt-in allowlisted repair subset rather than broad `doctor --fix`?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current read-only startup boundary, but automation cannot choose the product/security policy for unattended config mutation that can affect sandbox, auth/provider routing, plugins, and channel delivery.

options.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
options.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, and improve targeted doctor repair bugs and logging without automatic persistent startup writes.

options.title: Add Opt-In Safe Startup Repair
options.body: Define an allowlisted repair subset with backups, changed-path logging, and upgrade tests before exposing a named opt-in setting or setup choice.

options.title: Auto-Apply By Default
options.body: Apply safe repairs by default only if maintainers explicitly accept the compatibility and security risk and require broad upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
recommendation.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, and improve targeted doctor repair bugs and logging without automatic persistent startup writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-line and recent path-history signal across startup config, doctor flow, and docs for the policy boundary.
